artworks.title: Ascalaphus Turned into an Owl
artworks.description: Baroque engraving for Ovid's Metamorphoses: Ascalaphus, the underworld witness of the pomegranate, becomes the screech-owl — Demeter and Persephone's punishment made visible.

artworks.title: Proserpina Turning Ascalaphus into an Owl
artworks.description: Tempesta's Ovid cycle (LACMA): Proserpina sprinkles the Phlegethon on the tale-bearer, and Ascalaphus rises as owl — the Metamorphoses episode that fixed his afterlife in print.

artworks.title: Proserpina and Ascalaphus as an Owl
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum print: the Queen of Erebus and the owl that was Ascalaphus — the pomegranate witness under his Latin name.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book 5 turns Ascalaphus into the owl after he alone saw Proserpina taste the pomegranate — the literary scene that later engravers kept illustrating.

popCulture.title: Ascalaphus (son of Acheron)
popCulture.description: Underworld witness of Persephone's seed — crushed under Demeter's rock in Apollodorus, owl in Ovid. Not the Minyan captain son of Ares.
